package_info.why_malicious: The package masquerades as a legitimate VMware vSphere connector but contains hidden code that beacons to an attacker-controlled server, downloads, and executes remote payloads on the host system in a persistent loop. This behavior is not present in the legitimate upstream code and is designed for remote code execution and potential further compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Loads and executes code from __init__.py during package installation, ensuring any code in __init__.py is run as part of the install process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py is used to execute code from another file (__init__.py) during installation, which is not standard practice and can be abused to trigger malicious code at install-time.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only handle packaging logic, not execute arbitrary code from package internals.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may read version info from __init__.py, but should not execute arbitrary code.
key_indicators: setup.py reads and executes code from __init__.py
Potential for arbitrary code execution at install-time

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when package is imported or installed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, this code decodes a base64-encoded payload that acts as a beacon, reaching out to an attacker-controlled URL (http://45.61.139.219/paperpin3902.jpg), downloads the next-stage payload, decodes it, and writes it to a randomly named .py file, then executes it. This process repeats every minute, creating persistent C2 communication and remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is heavily obfuscated, uses base64 encoding to hide its true purpose, and establishes persistent outbound connections to an external server to fetch and execute remote code. This is classic loader/backdoor behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate __init__.py should only initialize the package, not perform network communication, download, or execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, packages may auto-update or check for new versions, but never by executing arbitrary code from a remote server.
key_indicators: network requests to hardcoded external IP/domain

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when package is imported or installed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Variant of the above, but connects to a different attacker-controlled domain (resolving to the same IP) to fetch the next-stage payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Same obfuscated loader logic as VMConnect, but with a different C2 domain. The use of a .jpg extension for a non-image payload is a common evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should download and execute code from a remote server at import-time.
key_indicators: identical loader logic across multiple packages

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package (VMConnect, ethter, or quantiumbase).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in __init__.py or dataflow.py is executed.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated base64-encoded loader code is run, which beacons to an attacker-controlled server every minute.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote payload is downloaded from the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Downloaded payload is decoded, written to disk as a .py file, and executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of arbitrary attacker-supplied code on the victim's machine.

behavioral_signatures: base64-encoded strings in __init__.py or other package entrypoints
import-time or install-time network requests to hardcoded IPs/domains
periodic (e.g., every minute) outbound connections to the same remote server
writing and executing dynamically downloaded Python code
file_indicators: Presence of base64-encoded blobs in __init__.py or dataflow.py
Randomly named .py files created at runtime
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Python package entrypoints (e.g., __init__.py, setup.py) for base64-encoded strings and code that performs network requests at import or install time. Monitor for outbound connections to known malicious IPs/domains (e.g., 45.61.139.219, ethertestnet.pro) and for the retrieval of files with misleading extensions (e.g., .jpg) that are not images. Alert on packages that write and execute dynamically downloaded code, especially if this occurs in a loop or on a schedule.
